title: The Death of the Author and Its Critics
text:
Roland Barthes's essay on the death of the author proposed that a text is not a message issued by a single creator but a tissue of quotations drawn from countless cultural sources. Once the writer's biography is set aside, the critic is freed from the search for a hidden intention and can attend to the play of signifiers on the page. Critics of this view, however, argued that dismissing the author entirely impoverishes the historical understanding of works and ignores the material conditions under which they were produced.

Feminist and postcolonial critics later complicated the picture by insisting that the question of who speaks is inseparable from the question of who is silenced. Their work revealed that canonical texts often encoded assumptions about race, gender, and empire that readers had long taken for granted as universal. Such revelations did not restore the author to a position of final authority, yet they made it harder to pretend that interpretation takes place in a neutral space.

questions.text: According to the passage, what does Barthes's essay propose a text is?
options: A message issued by one single creator
A tissue of quotations drawn from many cultural sources
A record of the author's private biography
A neutral document with no cultural origin

questions.text: What did later feminist and postcolonial critics insist?
options: That canonical texts are always politically neutral
That the question of who speaks is inseparable from who is silenced
That the author should regain final authority
That biography should be central to criticism

questions.text: What can be inferred about the critics who opposed Barthes's view?
options: They believed history and material conditions still matter to interpreting works
They wanted to return to reading texts only for their hidden intentions
They denied that texts are shaped by cultural sources
They thought the author's biography was irrelevant to all literature

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about the effect of postcolonial criticism on interpretation?
options: It made readers less likely to assume their own position is neutral
It proved that canonical texts are universal
It returned final authority to the author
It made literary study entirely subjective

paragraph_translations: Есей Ролана Барта про смерть автора стверджував, що текст є не повідомленням, яке надсилає один творець, а тканиною цитат, узятих із безлічі культурних джерел. Коли біографію письменника відкладено вбік, критик звільняється від пошуку прихованого наміру і може звернути увагу на гру означальників на сторінці. Однак противники цього погляду стверджували, що повне відкидання автора збіднює історичне розуміння творів і ігнорує матеріальні умови, за яких вони створювалися.

Феміністична та постколоніальна критика згодом ускладнила картину, наполягаючи на тому, що питання про те, хто говорить, нерозривно пов'язане з питанням про те, хто змушений мовчати. Їхня робота показала, що канонічні тексти часто закодовували припущення щодо раси, статі та імперії, які читачі давно сприймали як універсальні. Такі відкриття не повернули автору остаточної влади, але ускладнили вдавання, що інтерпретація відбувається в нейтральному просторі.
